dedupe_keys.name: fremont california solar and battery emergency microgrids at three fire stations

description: This case study documents solar emergency microgrids installed at three fire stations in Fremont, California. The project was led by Gridscape Solutions in partnership with the City of Fremont with 1.8 million dollars of grant funding from the California Energy Commission's Electric Program Investment Charge, and its final report was published in September 2019 as CEC-500-2019-054, free to download online as an 87-page PDF. Each microgrid combines a parking lot solar canopy, battery storage and an automated energy management system that runs the local resources both connected to the grid and islanded. Under a ten-year power purchase and energy savings agreement with the city, Gridscape continues to own, operate and maintain the systems. Coverage is three stations in one city. Caveats: savings and emission figures are the project's own estimates, and outage performance is stated as a design capability, not measured in a real disaster. The report states that each system can supply at least 4 to 6 hours of clean power during a utility outage, such as one caused by wildfire or earthquake, and estimates at least 250,000 dollars in energy savings over ten years and about 142,000 pounds of greenhouse gas reductions a year. Simulation uses: design parameters for backup power at emergency service facilities in outage and resilience models. Related records: the hospital microgrid designed with REopt (case_study-hospital-microgrid-reopt-grid-outage-resilience) and the CERTS microgrid test bed (data-certs-microgrid-test-bed) cover related designs.
